title: Fusarium wilt on African Eggplant, Cowpea and Pumpkin

Header: Fusarium wilt on African Eggplant, Cowpea and Pumpkin

Prevention: Rotate with non-solanaceaus species (Cereals, grasses) for longer seasons at least for 4 to 6 years because the fungus persist several in the soil for a long time
Remove and destroy all infested crop debris
Reduce the irrigation frequency and amount of water
Disinfect all pruning tools with 10% JIK Maintain high level of plant vigour with appropriate fertilization
Deeply plough the fields and leave them to fallow for 2-3 months where feasible
Monitoring: Keep on monitoring the field and look out for wilting plants.
Can be observed as slight vein clearing on outer leaflets and drooping of leaf petioles.
Lower leaves wilt, turn yellow and die
The entire plant may be killed, often before it reaches maturity.
In most cases a single-shoot wilts before the rest of the plant shows symptoms or one side of the plant is affected first.
Direct Control: Remove and destroy infected plant parts by burning or burying.
This will prevent the spread of the disease from spreading to neighbouring plants.
Spraying with fungicides will not control this disease.
The control of nematodes (especially root knot nematodes) is important as these interact positively with fusarium wilt and can lead to the loss of resistance in some cultivars.
Restrictions: Soil-borne disease so chemicals are not recommended.
